reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept the level-66 entry 66 data-name-1 RENAMES data-name-2 [THROUGH|THRU data-name-3]. with data-name-2/3 optionally qualified, and refuse a missing data-name-2, a dangling THRU, a second THRU, other clauses in the entry, a subscripted or reference-modified operand, a non-66 level and a missing or FILLER data-name-1; witnesses cover only clause repetition and a MOVE use.

reader.notes: RENAMES is a Nucleus level-2 element in 1985 and the compiler supports it unconditionally, as the full standard requires. An unqualified data-name-2 duplicated in another record is refused as non-unique (COBOL1639), consistent with SR5 and the 1985 uniqueness rules.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-001/: rn_d.cob (01 REC1. 05 A PIC X(2) VALUE "AA". 05 B PIC X(2). 66 R1 RENAMES A. 66 R2 RENAMES R1. DISPLAY R2) COMPILES AND RUNS at 85, printing AA; at --std 2002 and --std 2023 the same source is refused, COBOL1655 "'R1' does not name an item of the record". cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR4  the text is in SR4 ("A 66 level entry cannot rename another 66 level entry"). Mechanism: ResolveRedefinesPass.Run resolves data-name-2/3 through DataBinder.RegionClauseCandidates, which below 2002 (ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers false, kb/Work PB5165) returns QualifiedCandidates over the whole scope, so a level-66 alias (registered by BindRenames, Parent = the record) is a candidate and passes IsWithinRegion; ScreenRenamesOperand then tests only Level 1/77 and the owner, its comment stating levels 66 and 88 are 'off the storage tree and already unreachable (SR4)' -- true only on the 2002+ SubtreeCandidates arm. Other probes held: rn_a (A THRU G where G is the group containing A, and G THRU D over a fixed OCCURS between) compiles and prints AABB / AABBTTTDD, right by SR8 and SR3/SR6; rn_b (A THRU A), rn_c (G THRU B, dn3 subordinate), rn_e (RENAMES the 01), rn_f (range ends on an ODO table), rn_g (operand in an earlier record), rn_h (RENAMES an 88), rn_i (RENAMES a 77) are all refused. rn_d2 (66 R2 RENAMES A THRU R1; 66 R3 RENAMES R1 THRU C) is refused at 85 but with misleading messages (PB96 tiling, 'beginning of data-name-3 precedes'), since R1's offset is computed as if after the record's children.
